NO-SKIN feels like a Frankenstein's monster of "edgy" and "mysterious" indie horror games, and as someone who generally still appreciates the artistry and boundary-pushing of those games (even when they miss the mark), I unfortunately do not mean that as a good thing. My biggest issue with NO-SKIN is that it feels far too directionless; it's edgy for the sake of being edgy, and it's mysterious for the sake of being mysterious. This may not be the creator's intent, and I'm sure there is substance and underlying plot behind everything, but such a drip feed of actual narrative is provided that it ultimately feels purposeless.

I can prattle on for a bit on why this is, but let's first focus on the fact that we are immediately thrown into the Horror™. Before we even get a proper backstory or reason to care about the cast of characters at the beginning (who all make poor first impressions, by the way), we are just thrust straight into the fray. NOW, this is not inherently an issue by itself. It is a Roguelike after all, and having a long introductory cutscene or section would not work well either IMO. Also, other excellent games like Signalis and Silent Hill more or less do the same thing. The DIFFERENCE, is that those games give us far more to work with as the player progresses, and we are eventually given reason to care about the cast and also far more context on why the world is the way it is.

With NO-SKIN, even after almost 6 hours and beating the game multiple times (with nearly every run feeling nigh identical, even when factoring meta-progression and different playable characters), I still haven't the faintest clue about why I should give a damn about any of the side chars or Noire. I also finished all of the Dream Diaries up to Trish, and I still feel as if I know as much about Noire's "friends" as I did when I started my very first run. I finally gave in and decided to look at spoilers about the characters and all the endings, and I'm afraid to say that I neither care nor am able to empathize with literally anyone. 

And going back to my description of this game being a Frankenstein's monster, the world-building of this game does genuinely feel like that. It's an eldritch Lovecraft game where reality is an illusion, and the gods are inimical to humanity. It's also a meta-horror game where the video game is "aware" and the developer hates you!!! Also it's a psychological game about disastrous interpersonal relationships. Also there's dimensional hopping and alternate timeline stuff, and also it's Yume Nikki because everything might just be a dream, but also it isn't at all! And there's a bunch of quirky, Undertale-esque creatures to tie it all together!! Don't get me wrong, you can combine these concepts and create something that is both unique and memorable, but that still requires stable through lines that the narrative, on the surface, fundamentally lacks. And it is exponentially harder to weave these concepts together the more and more you stack on.

If I seem way too harsh in this review, I apologise, but part of why I am such is because I do see genuine potential both in this game and the abilities of the developer. To list the good things, I think the art-style is evocative; it's the main reason why I bought the game in the first place. I think the game-play was engaging - it's very simple at first (not a bad thing) and gets quite repetitive as runs pass, but with some more work and variation, it could stand on its own. Combat as both a puzzle and as a narrative tool is peak, and works especially well for turn-based Survival Horror. Also, I'm a massive sucker for religious horror and religious motifs in art, so that's a plus.

In summary, 2.5/5, I'll probably still end up copping Edenwound if / when it comes out since I do again see great potential, so hey, that's a win I suppose.

I have beaten the game two times now (I have not gotten the true ending), and after maybe the first 4 or 5 runs it starts to get repetitive. NO-SKIN's gameplay loop consists of room delving. Each room has a certain chance of a few different events happening, I think there's about 8-10 different rooms in total, with about 4.5 (I will explain what I mean by .5 later). events per room. This amount of variation seems fine at first, but it quickly devolves into monotony and in a weird way, a resource management game. 

Even with the max roguelite upgrades that the game gives you, which unlocks new rooms, there just isn't enough variety for this game to retain much replayability, especially when you find out that each area is just designated to give you certain things. Initially cool 1/10 or even 1/100 chance areas quickly become the "Oh the +12 fragments/1 medkit room", or the "Oh the funny dev joke room." The worst part about the outcomes of these rooms is that they're incredibly rare, and getting maybe a small tidbit of lore or a funny cutscene with no reward feels bad in a game that essentially becomes resource management after the player is familiarized with the gameplay loop. Because of these rooms being relatively useless/only slightly better than others, they feel like half rooms that pop in every once in awhile to slightly disrupt the gameplay loop. 


Besides my problems with events in the room design, the game does have a few pluses when it comes to combat. I love the artstyle of the various enemies and [spoiler] how they change as you get closer to NO SKIN /spoiler],  I also like the combat mechanics introduced throughout the game. However, again, I wish there were more enemies, or maybe that the enemies changed their attack patterns. Are you starting to see the common theme here?

The game lacks variety, which is key to replayability in a roguelite. The game needs more rooms and more events per room.  I honestly think that the base loop would be completely fine if it didn't have so little. I know it would make it harder to optimize runs, but maybe an item could be added that lets you increase your chances of getting into a certain room? 

Overall, the first few runs of the game feel great, and for $6 it honestly it isn't a bad price. If the gameplay loop was expanded upon and more variety was added this would be a great addition to the niche genre of horror roguelites alongside other similar games such as World of Horror.

The UI/UX is a complete mess—feels like no thought was given to the flow of interactions. Default keybinds are Z, X, and the arrow keys… Weird as hell. 

Dialogues repeat endlessly, and after the first time, you just don’t care anymore. But nope, you’re forced to fast-forward through them every single time, which makes up 95% of the game. This gets frustrating fast and even leads to misclicks from sheer boredom.

The story tries way too hard to be edgy, like it was written by some doomer who saw [i]Un Chien Andalou [/i] once—or just that one eyeball scene on YouTube—because, of course, there’s a weird reference to it in a cutscene featuring the dev’s webcam.

On the "bright side", the RNG is decent. Even if you get unlucky too many times in a row, there’s usually still a way to pull through. But honestly, this could have been a much better roguelike if the overall flow of gameplay was improved.
